answer: One concrete mechanism: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because quill only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, island is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any marble approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
